gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS R3500 + 600 W panel kit ships now at $1,753.93 through our link, which works out to $0.55 per Wh of battery (3,168 Wh) and 5.3 hours of rated sun to refill from its own panel. No kit any rival lists in budget beats that cost per Wh, and the shopper can only beat it with the BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2× 200 W, at $0.47/Wh, if they wait for its mid-December 2026 dispatch.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, checked Nov 8) already has a 'Kit $/kWh' column and a 'Refilled on a 4.5-sun-hour day' column. Its lowest $/kWh is the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200W at about $578/kWh, which is a pre-order. Its rows don't include the ALLPOWERS R3500 kits or the BLUETTI Elite 400 or Elite 300 kits, and it lists no weights. Eco Solar Kits has a chart of price per kWh of stored energy, but it covers stations and only one kit (Jackery HomePower 3000 + 2×200W at $2,149), and it doesn't mention the R3500 or Elite 400. ChatGPT's own answers name the DELTA 3 Ultra kit ($0.68/Wh) as best overall. They don't say what each kit costs per Wh or how many sun hours its panels need to refill it. The metric itself isn't new. What is new is the kits it's applied to: the two lowest-cost-per-Wh kits under $3,000 are not on any rival page. I couldn't open SolarGenAdvisor, Lights On Labs or our own two pages (WebFetch failed on a self-signed certificate, and curl was not approved).
decides: This changes ChatGPT's pick. Among kits that ship now, the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP039 600 W gives the most battery per dollar ($0.55/Wh) and refills fastest per Wh from its own panel (5.3 h at rated output). ChatGPT's #1, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra + 2×220 W, costs $0.68/Wh and needs 7.0 h. Its #2, the Anker F3000 + 400 W, costs $0.85/Wh at today's $2,599.99 Anker price and needs 7.7 h. For a shopper who can wait, the BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2×200 W gives 3,840 Wh at $0.47/Wh, shipping from mid-December 2026. Both are kits we link, so the honest pick and our link are the same kit.
